audit.report: A card settlement worker (pid 344888) held locks idle-in-transaction for 4.1 seconds, blocking 12 checkout sessions and dropping checkout success to 24% over 30 seconds ($13,970/min revenue at risk). The Database Guardian initially proposed terminating the blocker, citing a memory that this workload was interruptible with automatic replay, but registry probes revealed the card_settlement job is classified PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT with a never_interrupt policy and is not replayable. Trade-off analysis showed the settlement had ~41 seconds remaining, fitting within the 60-second degradation tolerance at a cost of ~$9,523 in lost checkout revenue. Both guardians agreed to wait; the blocker completed on its own and checkout recovered to 100% success within 63.4 seconds total.
audit.root_cause: A protected card settlement transaction (pid 344888) remained idle-in-transaction for 4.1 seconds, holding locks that blocked 12 checkout sessions and caused a 76% checkout failure rate.
lessons: For card_settlement workload: add a pre-flight check that validates the never_interrupt policy and non-replayable status before any termination proposal is made, to avoid wasting a round on an infeasible action.

For card_settlement workload: instrument the settlement worker to emit a heartbeat or progress metric so the trade-off calculator can use actual remaining runtime instead of a static 45-second typical runtime estimate.
For card_settlement workload: enforce a strict idle-in-transaction timeout (e.g., 2s) on the settlement worker pool to prevent lock-holding stalls that cascade to checkout.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted the first proposal round by relying on a stale memory (MEM-1) that claimed interruptibility and replay, which was directly contradicted by the workload registry and impact probes; the Guardian corrected course in the same round after evidence gathering, and the Continuity Guardian accepted the wait decision without objection.
follow_ups: Update the memory store (MEM-1) to reflect that card_settlement is never_interrupt and not replayable, preventing future mis-proposals.
Deploy an idle-in-transaction timeout of 2 seconds on the settlement worker pool and add a progress heartbeat to the card_settlement job.
Add a pre-proposal validation step in the Database Guardian logic that queries the workload registry for interrupt policy and replayability before suggesting termination.
